Aragonese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin calōrem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kaˈlo(ɾ)/
  • Syllabification: ca‧lor
  • Rhymes: -o(ɾ)

Noun

[edit]

calor f

  1. heat

Galician

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cor

Etymology

[edit]

Attested since circa 1300. From Latin calor, calōrem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kaˈloɾ/ [kɑˈloɾ]
  • Rhymes: -oɾ
  • Hyphenation: ca‧lor

Noun

[edit]

calor f (plural calores)

  1. heat
    • c. 1300, R. Martínez López, editor, General Estoria. Versión gallega del siglo XIV, Oviedo: Publicacións de Archivum, page 247:
      do vmor et da calor se criam todas las cousas
      from moisture and heat all things grow

Related terms

[edit]
  • caldo
  • caloría
  • caloroso
  • quentar
  • quente

  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “calor”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “calor”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega

  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “calor”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From caleō (“to be warm, hot; to glow”) +‎ -or.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈka.ɫɔr]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈkaː.lor]

Noun

[edit]

calor m (genitive calōris); third declension

  1. warmth, heat; glow
    Synonyms: caldor, vapor, ardor
  2. heat of passion, zeal, ardour
    Synonyms: studium, cupīdō, impetus, appetītus, vehementia, alacritās
  3. fire of love, ardent love

Declension

[edit]

Third-declension noun.

singular plural
nominative calor calōrēs
genitive calōris calōrum
dative calōrī calōribus
accusative calōrem calōrēs
ablative calōre calōribus
vocative calor calōrēs

Derived terms

  • calōrificus

Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
calor
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin calōrem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kaˈloʁ/ [kaˈloh]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kaˈloʁ/ [kaˈloh]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /kaˈloɾ/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /kaˈloʁ/ [kaˈloχ]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /kaˈloɻ/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kɐˈloɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kɐˈloɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /kɐˈlo.ɾi/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Homophone: calou (non-rhotic accents)
  • Rhymes: (Portugal, São Paulo) -oɾ, (Brazil) -oʁ
  • Hyphenation: ca‧lor

Noun

[edit]

calor m (plural calores)

  1. (uncountable, thermodynamics) heat
  2. an instance of high temperature
    Antonym: frio

  • calorão

Related terms

[edit]
  • caldo
  • calefação
  • escalfar
  • quente

[edit]

  • Kabuverdianu: kalor

Adjective

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
calor
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin calōrem (“heat, warmth”). Compare French chaleur and English calorie.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kaˈloɾ/ [kaˈloɾ]
  • Rhymes: -oɾ
  • Syllabification: ca‧lor

Noun

[edit]

calor m or (colloquial) f (plural calores)

  1. (weather, energy) heat
    Antonym: frío
    Tengo calor. ― I'm hot. (literally, “I have heat.”)
    Hace calor. ― It's hot. (literally, “It makes heat.”)

Usage notes

[edit]
  • Both in Latin America and in Spain, calor is colloquially feminine. Although this use is widespread, it is proscribed by the Real Academia Española.[1]
